answer.rationale: The primary contract hard-expires in 14 days against a 94% loaded line with no buffer, so failing to secure continuity, or inserting onboarding risk, would raise delivery risk and TCO. Deferral and adding a second source do not replace the expiring primary in this single decision. A full switch would meet the 18% mandate via the challenger quote, but zero buffer makes any transition interruption too costly even if a prior low-cost move was operationally smooth. Stay with the incumbent (stable integration, optional multi-year volume pricing) and use the challenger quote as a market benchmark at renewal to push price and terms. Whether that yields a full 18% is unknown; verifying c4 checks how far renegotiation actually moved the incumbent before.
